# Sovrium access and authentication options

> Generated from the Sovrium schema by scripts/build/generate-skill-references.ts — do not edit. It carries no version on purpose: when it and the binary you run disagree, the binary is right.

## `auth`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config auth` | object | Authentication configuration with strategies, roles, and plugins. Admin features are always enabled when auth is configured. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.allowSignUp` | boolean | Controls user self-registration. true allows anyone to sign up. false restricts user creation to admins. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.immediateAccountDeletion` | boolean | Lets a signed-in user delete their own account at once: they ask, a confirmation link is mailed to them, and following it erases the account and everything in it. Needs outgoing email. false closes this door; the scheduled deletion, erased after a 7-day grace period, stays available either way. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies` | array | Ways a person can sign in — email and password, a magic link, a one-time code, or an external provider. Each way may appear only once. May be empty or omitted when auth.sso declares at least one identity provider (an SSO-only app); otherwise at least one is required. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[]` | object | Authentication strategy configuration. Discriminated by `type` field: emailAndPassword, magicLink, or oauth. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].type` | enum | Which sign-in strategy this entry configures: emailAndPassword (an email and a password), magicLink (a one-time link sent by email) or oauth (a social provider such as Google or GitHub). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].minPasswordLength` | number | Minimum password length (6-128, default: 8) |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].maxPasswordLength` | number | Maximum password length (8-256, default: 128) |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].requireEmailVerification` | boolean | Require email verification before sign-in (default: false) |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].autoSignIn` | boolean | Auto sign in after signup (default: true) |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].expirationMinutes` | number | Link expiration time in minutes (default: 15) |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].providers` | array | OAuth providers to enable. Credentials loaded from environment variables. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.strategies[].providers[]` | enum | Supported OAuth providers for social login |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles` | array | Roles of your own, on top of the built-in admin, member and viewer. Each carries a level that decides what it inherits. A built-in role may also be listed, with nothing but a `defaultLanding` (and `pickerLanding`) or a `label`, to choose where it lands after signing in or what the console calls it. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[]` | object | Custom role definition with name, optional description, hierarchy level, and post-login landing rules. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].name` | string | Role name: lowercase, alphanumeric, hyphens. Must start with a letter. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].label` | string | What the console calls this role, in place of its name: the users directory, the invite dialog, the Change role picker and the account page show it. The name stays what permissions and writes use. Without a label the console uses its own words for a built-in role ("Admin (read-only)" for `admin-viewer`) and shows any other name made readable, `accounting-read` reading "Accounting read". A `$t:` key is translated in the operator's console language. A built-in role may be listed with only a label. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].description` | string | Human-readable description of the role |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].level` | number | Hierarchy level (higher = more permissions). Built-in: admin=80, member=40, viewer=10 |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].defaultLanding` | string | Where someone with this role is sent after signing in. It starts with `/`, and may carry one `$currentUser.assignments.<table>[0]` token to land them on their own record. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].pickerLanding` | string | Where someone with this role is sent instead when the landing token matches more than one record, so they can pick. It starts with `/` and carries no token. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].dashboardTier` | enum | Native Admin Dashboard access tier. admin-editor = full read + write (publish); admin-viewer = read-only. admin-editor ⊇ admin-viewer. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.roles[].canInvite` | boolean | Allows this role to invite users via POST /api/auth/admin/invite-user without being admin-equivalent. Absent means false. Does not lift the level ceiling (the invited role must be at or below this role) and does not cross tenants (the invitee inherits the inviter scope assignments). Denials remain 404. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.defaultRole` | string | Role assigned to new users by default. Must be a built-in role (`admin`, `member`, `viewer`) or a name declared in `auth.roles`; any other name, including the admin-tier names, fails validation at startup. Defaults to member. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.twoFactor` | boolean \| object | TOTP-based two-factor authentication |
| `sovrium docs config auth.twoFactor.issuer` | string | Issuer name shown in authenticator apps |
| `sovrium docs config auth.twoFactor.backupCodes` | boolean | Generate backup codes for recovery |
| `sovrium docs config auth.twoFactor.digits` | enum | Number of digits in TOTP code (6 or 8) |
| `sovrium docs config auth.twoFactor.period` | number | Code rotation period in seconds |
| `sovrium docs config auth.apiKeys` | boolean | Enable self-service API keys: a signed-in user can create, list and revoke their own keys and authenticate /api/* requests with the x-api-key header. Keys inherit their creator’s role. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.deviceAuthorization` | boolean | Let the sovrium CLI sign in with a short code approved in the browser: the CLI requests a code, a signed-in user approves it, and the CLI redeems it once for an API key of that user. Requires apiKeys: true. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates` | object | Templates for all authentication-related emails |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.verification` | object | Email template configuration with subject and body content. $variables are substituted where the email type provides them: $name, $email, $url, $otp, $codes, $organizationName, $inviterName, and $appName (the app name, in every email). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.verification.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.verification.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.verification.html` | string | HTML email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.resetPassword` | object | Email template configuration with subject and body content. $variables are substituted where the email type provides them: $name, $email, $url, $otp, $codes, $organizationName, $inviterName, and $appName (the app name, in every email). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.resetPassword.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.resetPassword.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.resetPassword.html` | string | HTML email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.magicLink` | object | Email template configuration with subject and body content. $variables are substituted where the email type provides them: $name, $email, $url, $otp, $codes, $organizationName, $inviterName, and $appName (the app name, in every email). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.magicLink.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.magicLink.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.magicLink.html` | string | HTML email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.emailOtp` | object | Email template configuration with subject and body content. $variables are substituted where the email type provides them: $name, $email, $url, $otp, $codes, $organizationName, $inviterName, and $appName (the app name, in every email). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.emailOtp.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.emailOtp.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.emailOtp.html` | string | HTML email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.twoFactorBackupCodes` | object | Email template configuration with subject and body content. $variables are substituted where the email type provides them: $name, $email, $url, $otp, $codes, $organizationName, $inviterName, and $appName (the app name, in every email). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.twoFactorBackupCodes.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.twoFactorBackupCodes.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |

| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.welcome.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.welcome.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.welcome.html` | string | HTML email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.accountDeletion` | object | Email template configuration with subject and body content. $variables are substituted where the email type provides them: $name, $email, $url, $otp, $codes, $organizationName, $inviterName, and $appName (the app name, in every email). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.accountDeletion.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.accountDeletion.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.accountDeletion.html` | string | HTML email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.invitation` | object | Email template configuration with subject and body content. $variables are substituted where the email type provides them: $name, $email, $url, $otp, $codes, $organizationName, $inviterName, and $appName (the app name, in every email). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.invitation.subject` | string | Email subject line with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.invitation.text` | string | Plain text email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.emailTemplates.invitation.html` | string | HTML email body with optional $variable substitution |
| `sovrium docs config auth.invitationTokenExpiry` | string \| number | Lifetime of single-use admin invitation tokens. Defaults to 72h when omitted. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso` | array | Identity providers users can sign in with, over OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0. Declared in config only — providers cannot be registered at runtime. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[]` | object | One single sign-on identity provider. type oidc takes an oidc block, type saml a saml block. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].id` | string | Stable identifier of the identity provider, used in its callback URL. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Changing it breaks the redirect URI registered at the provider. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].type` | enum | The protocol: oidc (OpenID Connect) or saml (SAML 2.0). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].label` | string | The text of the sign-in button for this provider. Supports $t:key translation references. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].domains` | array | Email domains this provider is authoritative for. A sign-in that starts from an email address in one of them is routed here, and an existing account with such an address is linked on first SSO sign-in. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].domains[]` | string | An email domain, lowercase, without the @ (e.g. acme.com). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc` | object | OpenID Connect settings for an identity provider of type oidc. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.issuer` | string | The issuer URL. Endpoints and signing keys are discovered from <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration, and the ID token issuer must equal it. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.clientId` | string | The client id issued by the provider. Not a secret; may be a literal or an $env. reference. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.clientSecret` | string | The client secret issued by the provider, as an $env. reference. A literal is refused. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.scopes` | array | Scopes requested at the authorization endpoint. openid is always sent, whether listed or not. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.scopes[]` | string | One scope. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.pkce` | boolean | Send a PKCE (S256) code challenge with the authorization request. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.claimMapping` | object | Which claims carry the email, display name and picture, when the provider does not use the standard email, name and picture. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.claimMapping.email` | string | The claim holding the email address. Map only a claim your provider verifies: an existing account is linked only when the provider asserts email_verified. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.claimMapping.name` | string | The claim holding the display name. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].oidc.claimMapping.image` | string | The claim holding the picture URL. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml` | object | SAML 2.0 settings for an identity provider of type saml: metadata, or entityId + entryPoint + cert. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.metadata` | string | The identity provider metadata XML, inline or as an $env. reference. When set, entityId, entryPoint and cert are read from it. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.entityId` | string | The identity provider entity id (its Issuer). Required without metadata. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.entryPoint` | string | The identity provider single sign-on URL the browser is sent to. Required without metadata. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.cert` | string | The identity provider signing certificate (PEM), inline or as an $env. reference. Responses not signed by it are refused. Required without metadata. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.spEntityId` | string | The entity id Sovrium announces as service provider, and the audience assertions must carry. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.attributeMapping` | object | Which assertion attributes carry the email and the name. Without it the email is read from the email attribute (else the NameID), and the name from firstName and lastName (else displayName). |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.attributeMapping.email` | string | The attribute holding the email address. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.attributeMapping.name` | string | The attribute holding the display name. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.attributeMapping.firstName` | string | The attribute holding the first name. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].saml.attributeMapping.lastName` | string | The attribute holding the last name. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].roleMapping` | object | Map a claim or attribute to a Sovrium role. Applied at every sign-in, so the identity provider stays the source of truth. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].roleMapping.claim` | string | The claim or attribute holding the value to map — a string, or a list such as groups. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].roleMapping.map` | object | Claim value → role name. Entries are tried in the order written; the first value the user carries decides. Only an entry written here can grant an admin role. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].roleMapping.default` | string | The role given when no entry matches. Never an admin role. Defaults to auth.defaultRole. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.sso[].allowSignUp` | boolean | Whether a first sign-in creates an account. false admits only accounts that already exist — invited, created by an admin, or provisioned through SCIM. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.passkeys` | boolean \| object | Passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in. A signed-in user registers a passkey, then signs in with it without a password. The relying party is derived from BASE_URL. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.passkeys.rpName` | string | The name an authenticator shows when it saves the passkey. Defaults to the app name. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.passkeys.requireForAdmin` | boolean | Admit an admin-tier account to the admin plane only from a session it opened with a passkey. Its password session can still register one. Over MCP, the admin-only tools need an OAuth token authorised from a passkey session; an API key never qualifies. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.scim` | object | SCIM 2.0 user and group provisioning under /api/scim/v2/, authenticated by a bearer token from the environment. Deactivating a user signs them out and blocks sign-in; it erases nothing. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.scim.token` | string | The bearer token the identity provider sends, as an $env. reference. Any other token answers 404. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.scim.providers` | array | The auth.sso providers provisioned accounts sign in through. A provisioned account and the SSO identity with the same email are one account. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.scim.providers[]` | string | Stable identifier of the identity provider, used in its callback URL. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Changing it breaks the redirect URI registered at the provider. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.presence` | object | App-wide presence: who is online, when each person was last seen, and who is typing, shown only to the roles named in visibleTo and never to anonymous visitors. Without it, only page presence (a page’s presence: true) exists. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.presence.visibleTo` | array | The roles that see who is online, their last-seen time when lastSeen is on, and who is typing when typing is on. A reader of any other role receives none of it and is not told it exists; an anonymous visitor never receives it. At least one role. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.presence.visibleTo[]` | string | A role, built in or declared under auth.roles. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.presence.lastSeen` | boolean | Keep, per person, the time one of her realtime connections last closed, read as lastSeen on the account directory (GET /api/users/directory) by the roles in visibleTo while she is offline. Not filterable or sortable, and not on user fields. It is personal data: listed in her account export and deleted with her account. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.presence.typing` | boolean | Relay typing signals between the readers of one record whose role is in visibleTo: the server passes on who is writing under that record, to those readers only. A composer that sends these signals and an "is typing" label that shows them are part of the conversation components. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.groups` | array | User groups for permission grouping. Referenced in permissions with group: prefix. Teams are configured through groups. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.groups[]` | object | User group for RBAC grouping. Groups provide many-to-many user-to-group membership, referenced in permissions with the group: prefix. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.groups[].name` | string | Group identifier. Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.groups[].label` | string | What the console calls this group, in place of its name: the users directory and the Change groups picker show it. The name stays what permissions (`group:<name>`) and the membership write use. Without a label the console shows the name made readable, `equipe-a` reading "Equipe a". A `$t:` key is translated in the operator's console language. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.groups[].description` | string | Human-readable description of the group purpose |
| `sovrium docs config auth.groups[].maxMembers` | number | Maximum number of users allowed in this group (min 1, unlimited if omitted) |
| `sovrium docs config auth.scopeTables` | array | Tables that user_access rows can reference for multi-tenant scoping. Validated against app.tables[].name at startup. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.scopeTables[]` | string | Table slug from app.tables[].name (e.g., "clients", "projects") |
| `sovrium docs config auth.landingPath` | string | Engine-resolver mount path. Sessions navigating here are redirected to the matching role.defaultLanding. Must start with /. Must be backed by a co-located page declaration that acts as the unauthenticated-access guard. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.noAccessPath` | string | Fallback path when no role.defaultLanding matches the session. Defaults to /403. |
| `sovrium docs config auth.loginPage` | string | Path of the app’s sign-in page. Every engine redirect that sends a signed-out visitor to sign in lands here, carrying the way back. An app-relative path: it starts with a single / and carries no host, query or fragment. |

## `pages[].access`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config pages[].access` | enum \| array \| object | Page access control. 'all' (public), 'authenticated' (logged-in), role array ['admin'], or extended { require, redirectTo }. |
| `sovrium docs config pages[].access.require` | enum \| array | Permission value for a single operation. 'all' (everyone), 'authenticated' (logged-in users), or role array ['admin', 'editor']. |
| `sovrium docs config pages[].access.require[]` | string | One role name that has access — a built-in role or one declared in `auth.roles`. |
| `sovrium docs config pages[].access.redirectTo` | string | Path a visitor who has not signed in is sent to. A signed-in person without the required role is answered 404, never redirected. |

## `forms[].access`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].access` | object | Access control for a form. Reuses the shared permission model. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].access.require` | enum \| array | Permission value for a single operation. 'all' (everyone), 'authenticated' (logged-in users), or role array ['admin', 'editor']. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].access.require[]` | string | One role name that has access — a built-in role or one declared in `auth.roles`. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].access.redirectTo` | string | URL path to redirect unauthenticated/unauthorized submitters |

## `forms[].antiSpam`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].antiSpam` | object | Anti-spam controls for form submissions (honeypot, rate-limit) |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].antiSpam.honeypot` | boolean | When true, server adds a hidden honeypot field; bots that fill it are blocked |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].antiSpam.rateLimit` | object | Rate-limit configuration for form submissions |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].antiSpam.rateLimit.perIp` | number | Maximum submissions per IP within the time window |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].antiSpam.rateLimit.perForm` | number | Maximum submissions per form (all IPs) within the time window |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].antiSpam.rateLimit.windowSeconds` | number | Rolling time window in seconds for rate-limit counting |

## `forms[].availability`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability` | object | When the form accepts answers: an opening date, a closing date, a cap on the number of submissions, and what to show once it is closed. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.opensAt` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp at which the form opens for submissions |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closesAt` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp at which the form closes |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.maxSubmissions` | number | Maximum number of submissions accepted before the form auto-closes |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closedPage` | object | Custom closed-form UI block (title, message, optional CTA link) |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closedPage.type` | enum | How a closed form answers. `page` — the only shape — draws the notice below in place of the form. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closedPage.title` | string | Heading shown to a visitor who arrives while the form is closed. Accepts a `$t:` key. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closedPage.message` | string | Text explaining why the form is closed, and what to do instead. Accepts a `$t:` key. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closedPage.cta` | object | An optional link offered to a visitor who arrives while the form is closed. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closedPage.cta.label` | string | Text of the link offered on the closed-form page. Accepts a `$t:` key. |
| `sovrium docs config forms[].availability.closedPage.cta.href` | string | Where that link goes. An `http://` or `https://` address, or a path on this site (`/thanks`, `thanks`, `?sent=1`, `#done`). Any other address — `javascript:`, `data:`, `mailto:`, or one starting with `//` — is refused when the config is read. |

## `tables[].aiAccess`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess` | boolean \| object | Per-entity declaration of MCP/AI exposure intent. Boolean shorthand (true = enabled with defaults) or rich config object. Schema author declares; operator activates via MCP_ENABLED env var. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.description` | string | Hand-written description shown to the AI client. Overrides auto-generated descriptions. The single biggest UX lever for steering AI behavior — explain when to use this tool, what context the AI needs, and any non-obvious constraints. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.operations` | array | Subset of CRUD operations to expose. Defaults to all 5 (read, list, create, update, delete) for tables. Automations and actions ignore this field — they expose a single invocation tool. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.operations[]` | enum | One CRUD operation to expose as a tool — `read` and `list` are the two reads, `create`, `update` and `delete` the three writes. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.fieldExposure` | enum | Field exposure mode. Defaults to permissioned (only fields the connecting role can read/write per RBAC). |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.whitelistFields` | array | Fields to expose when fieldExposure=whitelist. Required and must be non-empty when fieldExposure=whitelist; ignored otherwise. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.whitelistFields[]` | string | One field name to expose, spelled as the table declares it. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations` | object | Risk hints exposed to MCP clients to drive auto-approve vs. confirmation UX. Optional; sensible defaults are derived from the operation type when unset. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.readOnly` | boolean | Marks the table's tools as read-only for MCP clients (readOnlyHint), which may then run them without asking. Applies only when every exposed operation is read or list; on a table that also exposes create, update or delete, read tools are always read-only and write tools never are, whatever this says. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.destructive` | boolean | Tool performs destructive operations (delete, send email, charge card); clients should require explicit confirmation. Maps to MCP destructiveHint. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.idempotent` | boolean | Calling the tool twice with the same args is safe (no duplicate side effects). Maps to MCP idempotentHint. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.openWorld` | boolean | Tool reaches outside the local app (external API, network call). Maps to MCP openWorldHint. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.requireConfirmation` | boolean | Force destructiveHint=true on the resulting MCP tool regardless of operation type. Use for automations/actions whose effects are non-reversible (e.g. sending emails) even if technically idempotent. |

## `agents[].permissions`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions` | object | RBAC integration model for AI agents. Agents are stored as auth.user records with type=agent and inherit role-based permissions. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions.type` | enum | User type discriminator — always 'agent' for AI agents |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions.trigger` | enum \| array | Who can trigger this agent. 'all', 'authenticated', or role array ['admin', 'member']. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions.trigger[]` | string | One role name that has access — a built-in role or one declared in `auth.roles`. |

## `env[]`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config env[]` | object | Environment variable definition for use in automation actions |
| `sovrium docs config env[].key` | string | Environment variable key (uppercase snake_case, e.g., API_KEY) |
| `sovrium docs config env[].description` | string | Description of what this env var is used for |
| `sovrium docs config env[].required` | boolean | Whether this variable must be set. Defaults to true: an unset required variable refuses to boot. |
| `sovrium docs config env[].default` | string | Default value used when the environment variable is not set. If both required and default are provided, default acts as fallback. |
| `sovrium docs config env[].secret` | boolean | Whether `default` holds a credential. Defaults to TRUE — omit it and the default is redacted wherever the config is reflected to an operator. Set `secret: false` to let a harmless default (a port, a region, a base URL) render verbatim in the configuration-as-booted view of the admin console (/_admin/changelog?view=current) instead of ***. |
